items.title: AIHOT
items.description: 一个自己找热点、自己写日报的网站框架。把信源和精选标准换成你的，它就是你的行业热点站。
items.summary: AIHOT is a website framework designed to help users find industry hot topics and write daily reports by themselves. It allows users to replace the source feeds and selection criteria with their own, transforming it into a personalized industry hot spot station. The platform aggregates information from 168 carefully selected sources, categorized into T1, T1.5, and T2 based on their reliability and relevance. It uses an embedding technique to cluster semantically similar entries and selects the most authoritative one as the main article. The AIHOT also features an AI daily report function that compiles the past 24 hours of selected content into a daily report categorized into five sections: model/product updates, industry dynamics, research papers, and tips/opinions. The daily report generation process is efficient, taking only one second per day, and does not rely on large models for content selection, categorization, or translation.

items.title: jevgrep
items.description: Find code by asking what it does. A CLI for coding agents that uses Jev to discover relevant files and source context.
items.summary: Jevgrep is a command-line tool designed to help coding agents by using Jev to discover relevant files and source context in one response, thus reducing the token cost of navigating unfamiliar repositories. It is invoked as `jg` and takes a question about a repository to return relevant files, search leads, and verbatim source excerpts. According to David on X, Jevgrep reduces coding agent cost by 40% as verified on SWE-bench. The tool aims to compress the exploration process into a single step, allowing coding agents to move directly toward implementation and testing instead of spending time reconstructing the repository's structure through repeated searches.

The project is self-hostable, MIT-licensed, and built with CopilotKit and AG-UI. It includes features like voice calls, Slack collaboration, and Spaces and Pages for document work. items.title: onetake
items.description: Motion films that never cut to the next slide: every beat grows out of the one before, one continuous camera, continuity measured by an oracle. A Claude Agent Skill for product launch films and feature demos.
items.summary: onetake is a motion film technology that creates continuous-camera product launch films and feature demos without cuts between scenes. It uses a continuous virtual camera that follows transformations without cutting, ensuring each beat grows out of the previous one. The technology employs an oracle script to score transition continuity, rejecting films that do not meet the threshold before human review. It reconstructs interfaces in HTML and uses deterministic motion rules to maintain visual continuity and reproducibility. The technology is a deterministic motion-design pipeline for personal, academic, and amateur work, not a general commercial video generator.

items.title: strands-decider
items.description: A small, fast decision model, or system one model, for agentic workflows. Pick between options or rate on a scale faster than an LLM, with a calibrated confidence on every decision.
items.summary: Strands Decider 2B is a small, fast decision model designed to run locally and return confidence-scored choices in tens–low hundreds of milliseconds. It is open source, with weights and training scripts published, and is part of a new class of decision models or system one models that are gaining attention. Unlike large language models (LLMs), decision models are designed to pick between sets of options and assign simple numerical scores, making them perfect for agentic workflows like agent routing, guardrails, and tool selection. They are faster, more capable at a given size, always produce an answer from selected options, and can run with very low latency, though they are not suited for complex problem-solving or text generation tasks.

items.title: ten-levels-of-jev
items.description: Ten levels of Jev, from one smart if statement to a coding agent that reaches for Jev on its own
items.summary: The sources describe ten levels of Jev, starting from simple smart if statements to a coding agent that autonomously decides when to call Jev. Levels 1 to 5 call Jev from code, while levels 6 to 10 integrate Jev into the Pi coding agent, with each level giving the agent more autonomy over the questions. Levels 6 and 7 act as hooks, running at the tool call, tool result, and turn end without the agent asking questions. Levels 8, 9, and 10 are tools that the agent decides to call, with level 10 allowing the agent to write its own Jev questions to classify test failures and check fixes. The YouTube video by IndyDevDan elaborates on how Jev is changing agentic engineering by keeping the coding agent for hard work and giving narrow decisions to a system one model like Jev.

items.summary: TIRx Harness is an open-source compiler harness designed for agentic GPU programming, combining a minimal stable compiler foundation, a knowledge base, tools, and a benchmark server to help agents develop correct, fast GPU kernels. It is built on Apache TVM and targets fast-moving ML kernels and hardware. On evaluated workloads, Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) kernels achieve geometric-mean speedups of 2.94× over FlashKDA (forward) and 6.84× over Flash Linear Attention (FLA) (backward). items.title: remocn-studio
items.description: Agent-native video editor
items.summary: The remocn-studio Agent-native video editor does not require any external video editing software like After Effects. It operates entirely in the browser with an AI agent that builds the demo video from ready-made pieces based on a description provided by the user. The process involves no keyframes, timelines, or learning curve for traditional video editing. Instead, users describe their desired video, and the agent constructs it using pre-built components. The Remotion framework is used for creating videos as code, and the agent executes the video creation in a remote machine environment once the user approves the creative plan.

items.title: ufo-core
items.description: Agent operating system
items.summary: The UFO-core Agent operating system is described as a next-generation agent operating system built by the creators of GitHub Copilot and Perplexity Computer. It features a logo-centric UI with an LLM-driven AgentOS Core, event-aware Python hooks, and runs atop existing operating systems via Electron with a Python backend. The system is designed to learn and adapt to a company's specific needs and workflows.

items.title: dsh-jev-plugin
items.description: Native DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin integrating TypeSafe Jev as a System One decision layer for agent selection, supervision, corrections, and approvals.
items.summary: The dsh-jev-plugin integrates TypeSafe Jev as a decision layer for DeepSeek Harness (DSH), focusing on agent selection, supervision, corrections, and approvals. The latest version available as of 2026-09-23 is `0.1.4`, which installs with `@buberlo/jev-core@^0.1.4`. Versions `0.1.2` and `0.1.3` are broken and should not be installed. The plugin enhances DSH by reducing supervision friction, keeping files, previews, terminal activity, and Git context closer to the conversation where the agent is working. It does not improve the model's coding abilities but extends DSH by aligning with its rapidly changing developer-preview platform.
